title: AIPCon 9 — Palantir AIP operational intelligence

corroboratingSources.purpose: Corroborates selected AIPCon 9 customer outcomes and operational themes.

signals.assessment: AIP agents are being positioned as governed execution layers for high-friction enterprise workflows, including ERP and cloud migration rather than chat-only assistance.
signals.basis: Palantir first-party Q1 2026 business update describing AIPCon 9 customer deployment outcomes.

signals.assessment: Palantir reported early SAP-cloud migration engagements above 99% validation accuracy within two weeks and more than 70% timeline and cost reduction.
AIP is being used in fleet-management and supply-chain workflows; GE Aerospace reported materially higher engine output in 2025 while presenting its Palantir-enabled operational transformation.

blackHouseImplications: Treat AIP as a governed operational execution layer connected to ontology objects, actions, evidence, and approvals.
Prefer measurable workflow outcomes over generic model capability claims.
Model migration, validation, supply-chain, fleet, and other operational workflows as ontology-backed missions with explicit evidence.
Keep external video intelligence supplemental until reconciled with Palantir documentation or other first-party evidence.
Never infer external authorization, partnership, customer status, or deployment rights from public AIPCon material.
